correctness.rationale: For b>=2, cancellation and reduction modulo odd p gives p|(b-1), and derivative ratio below 2 forces a=t=1,b=p+1; then derivative parity of 2u contradicts p-1. With b=1, exact quotient equation and the odd parity of p force t<=2, a=2 and precisely the stated D(u) equations. Direct reversal proves sufficiency. The squarefree conclusion is proved using q|D(u) whenever q^2|u. Verifier checked 21,172 two-support integers through 200,000; this is corroboration only.

value.rationale: The cototient-derivative equation has natural known witnesses but no evident unrestricted two-prime-support reduction. This theorem rules out all repeated odd prime factors and every even exponent except 2, then locates all remaining uncertainty in two natural reciprocal-sum equations, one connected to unresolved odd primary pseudoperfect numbers. The structural reduction across an infinite prime/exponent family is useful independently of the unsolved enumeration of the two auxiliary branches.
